chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from 'Umar ibn Yazeed from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him about a mother of the child (umm al-walad) being sold for debt; he said: 'Yes, for the price of her neck (slavery).'

key_terms.أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ: A concubine who has borne her master a child, gaining specific legal status
key_terms.رَقَبَتِهَا: Her neck, referring to her status as a slave/servant

ai.seo_question: Can an umm al-walad be sold to pay off her master's debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial liability of an 'umm al-walad' in Shia jurisprudence, confirming that her sale to settle a master's debt is valid provided the proceeds are applied to her manumission price. It highlights the practical application of property rights over concubines in early Islamic society, linking the concept of debt settlement directly to the valuation of her freedom. The chain of transmission through prominent Kufan narrators underscores the reliability of this ruling within the Usuli tradition.
